messages:
maria: Quick question from AcmeBank POC — they want to upload sample customer records during the POC. Do we treat that as in-scope for ISO/ISMS? Also they asked about KMS ownership and whether we can enforce a 30-day retention/deletion. cc @leo @june

leo: Short answer: if real customer PII is processed in the POC on hosted trial accounts, we should treat it as in-scope for controls that touch data (encryption, access, retention). If the POC is synthetic data only, it can remain out-of-scope. Need the dataflow to be sure. :mag_right:

maria: They plan to use our hosted API (trial account) with a CSV upload via the web UI. Data will include names, emails, support notes (PII-ish). No dedicated VPC or private deployment. They specifically asked: can we guarantee deletion after 30 days and can they bring their own KMS?

leo: Hosted trial = we do NOT support customer-managed KMS. For hosted mode we use Redwood-managed KMS. We can commit to deletion policies (we have retention deletes) but that needs to be reflected in the DPA/SOW and operational runbook. If they require customer-managed keys or private networking, they'd need Dedicated or Private deployment.

june: Adding from security: We can accept POC with customer data only under these pre-reqs: 1) DPA signed before ingestion, 2) explicit retention SLA (30d is OK), 3) written confirmation of PII minimization, and 4) security onboarding checklist completed by infra team. For hosted mode: customer keys not supported; for Private mode we can accept customer KMS/CMKs and document key handling in onboarding.

maria: Can you provide a short applicability snippet I can paste into the SOW so legal + the customer have something concrete?

leo: Paste this into SOW (short):

```
Applicability: Redwood Inference's ISO 27001 ISMS covers production services and customer data processed in Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted trial accounts are excluded from the ISMS scope for customer-managed infrastructure and customer-managed keys unless a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and a documented onboarding process are executed. For POCs that involve customer data in hosted mode, the following conditions must be met prior to ingestion: DPA signed; retention period capped at 30 days (or as agreed); customer acknowledges that Redwood-managed KMS will be used for hosted trial data. For Private deployments, customer-managed KMS is supported and will be validated as part of onboarding controls.
```

maria: Nice — that reads well. One more: Acme's security team asked for evidence mapping for controls around encryption at rest and key rotation. Can we share the relevant control mapping now or do we need a formal request?

june: We can share a high-level control applicability table (non-sensitive). I'll point them to the public/partner-friendly docs and offer to send the ISO evidence pack under NDA. High-level bullets: AES-256 at rest; keys in AWS KMS (Redwood-managed) for hosted; CMK support for Private; rotation policy: annual rotation for CMKs, with key policy audits and access logging via CloudTrail.

june: Internal link for sales/legal to reference (do not share externally without NDA): https://redwood.internal/docs/iso-evidence-pack

security-bot: Reminder — do NOT upload or paste any sensitive evidence into public Slack channels. Use secure-share or the SRM portal for external transfers.

maria: Got it. I'll send the snippet + the high-level bullets to Acme, request DPA, and loop legal for the formal evidence request. Thanks all! :heart:
